name: psrr-vs-freq
description: PSRR vs frequency at the ratified binding light-load condition (1 mA), 1kHz and 100kHz spec points called out
claim: README.md Target specification, 'PSRR' row (DR-0004 amendment A7): >50dB @ 1kHz (binding -- light load, per note 1) and >20dB @ 100kHz, at Iload=1mA, C_eff=1uF nominal. This deck covers the 1 mA condition ONLY. The 50 mA condition the ratified row also names is run as its own sibling experiment, sim/psrr-vs-freq-50ma/ (#99), because the two DC bias points cannot share one deck -- see tb_psrr.spice's header comment for the ngspice limitation (per-.meas result vectors go out of scope as soon as a later analysis becomes the current plot, so an 'alter'-and-re-.ac deck silently re-reports the first .ac's numbers instead of erroring). The two load conditions therefore carry two records with two separate verdicts, and are never merged into one. Records minted from this deck before 2026-08-16 predate the Mrza/Rza adaptive-compensation shelf that PR #78 / DR-0015 landed in design/error_amp.sch, so their DUT netlist sha no longer matches design/netlist/ldo_core.spice -- the staleness #95's T1/bronze re-read found and #99 closes; each refresh mints a new record naming the one it supersedes, and the superseded records stay untouched per the append-only rule. Harness integrity: the load sink is compliance-limited (see tb_psrr.spice and sim/harness/README.md, 'Compliance-limited load sinks') -- it draws its commanded current for VOUT well above ground and nothing at or below ground, which is what any real load does, and which deletes the sink-sustained unphysical DC solution #40 found (pass device off, the sink holding VOUT tens of volts BELOW ground through forward-biased substrate junctions in the PDK device models, with everything the .ac then reported a small-signal expansion about that root) rather than biasing the solver away from it. At the reported operating point the sink is an ideal current sink to within 1.3e-14 relative error and presents under 5.1e-16 S of small-signal conductance at 1 mA -- an open circuit at AC, exactly like the ideal sink it replaces -- and dc_vout_v / dc_iload_ma below read the .op plot so the operating point this PSRR is expanded about is reported and checked at every corner. That .op is reporting only, not steering: ngspice's ac command solves its own operating point, and the fix was confirmed order-independent by hand at tt_27c_3.30v (#46) -- running ac cold with no preceding op gives PSRR@1kHz = -25.2 dB with the old ideal sink (an expansion about the sub-ground root) and +77.91 dB with this sink, the latter identical to the op-then-ac ordering. No ratified threshold was changed. Update (#174, 2026-09-05, spec/decision-records/DR-0021): ldo_core's VREF was promoted from an internal net -- driven by Vref1, an ideal 1.2 V vsource instantiated INSIDE the subcircuit -- to a seventh top-level port, and the identical ideal source moved into this deck. No device was added, removed or resized, so this is an electrical no-op by construction: an ideal vsource is an ideal vsource wherever it is declared, its return was already the cell's VSS port, and it is an AC short to ground in both placements. It is not asserted on that argument alone -- origin/main at ec9e530 was extracted to a scratch tree and this bench was run on BOTH trees back to back, on the same host with the same ngspice and the same pinned PDK, and the per-corner measurement lines compared field by field; DR-0021's 'Evidence' section tabulates the result. Records minted from this deck before 2026-09-05 carry the pre-#174 six-port DUT netlist sha and are superseded on that ground alone, not because any number in them was wrong; per sim/README.md's append-only rule they are left untouched. Update (#304, 2026-09-23): the 'deletes' sentence above is scoped deliberately -- the compliance bound deletes the SINK-SUSTAINED sub-ground root and nothing else. Below the knee the sink is exactly 0 A and 0 S (f(VOUT) underflows to 0.0 in IEEE double for every VOUT <= -0.7530773732699249 V), so the load network is absent from the DC equations there: a sub-ground dc_vout_v reported together with dc_iload_ma = 0 is outside the sink's reach by construction, and no knee or softness value can delete it because the sink has no term left in the equations to remove. Record 20260923-084323-a6c95f8 reported exactly that at fs_125c_3.63v (dc_vout_v = -64.75 V, dc_iload_ma = 0, psrr_1k_db = 0.0013) on the DUT netlist of the day; #304 measured the mechanism and it is NOT a second physical solution but a false convergence on the continuation ladder's first rung (dynamic gmin stepping), accepted by SPICE's RELATIVE convergence test 64 V from ground -- seeded on the state it is accepted at reltol=1e-3 and evaporates at 1e-4/1e-5/1e-6, the reported value moves with the seed by about reltol*|V| (65 mV), and every element attached to VOUT is evaluated as feeding current INTO it while the only element that could absorb any is evaluated at exactly 0 A. Both harness-integrity checks below caught it, which is what they are for. The deck is deliberately unchanged on that account: knee tuning is coin-flipping (a strictly LOOSER bound 'fixes' the same corner, so the knee is not the mechanism) and a load-side sub-ground clamp is worse still -- measured, it creates a genuine root at VOUT = -0.4994 V that a cold start reaches. See sim/harness/README.md, 'What the bound cannot reach', for the evidence and the reltol-ladder recipe that distinguishes a false convergence from a genuine second root.
analyses: meas ac vout_1k FIND vdb(vout) AT=1k
meas ac vout_100k FIND vdb(vout) AT=100k

operating_conditions.load_current: 1 mA (binding light-load condition per README.md note 1), commanded through a compliance-limited sink (Vilc/Bload/Vlmeas) and verified by dc_iload_ma
operating_conditions.output_cap: 1.0 uF nominal + 100 mOhm ESR (PSRR row's stated C_eff)
operating_conditions.enable_state: enabled (EN tied to VIN at instantiation)

psrr_1k_db.description: README.md PSRR target: >50 dB @ 1 kHz (binding light-load point)

dc_iload_ma.description: Harness integrity, not a ratified spec line: the compliance-limited sink must deliver the commanded 1 mA at the operating point this .ac is expanded about (see Claim)

dc_vout_v.description: Harness integrity, not a ratified spec line (the ratified accuracy row is sim/mc-output-accuracy's): asserts the .ac was linearized about the physical operating point, not the sub-ground root #40 found nor the sub-ground false convergence #304 characterised. Read it together with dc_iload_ma, which discriminates the two: the commanded current means a sink-sustained root, zero means a state the compliance bound could never have deleted
